To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

blood vessel wall cells and blood components, including platelets and leukocytes, interact with one another and with materials in ways that contribute to the formation of vascular lesions that limit the success of certain cardiovascular therapeutic interventions.
blood-biomaterial interactions modulate the function of vascular wall cells, and that such modulations contribute to the development of vascular lesions.
the interactions among cells of the vessel wall, the blood, and materials probably play a significant role in the formation and progression of vascular lesion formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathobiology of vascular lesion formation.
the pathobiology of vascular lesion formation and the mechanisms of vascular complications.
understanding the interactions between blood and the blood vessel wall that contribute to vascular lesion formation and late complications of these lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactions between blood and the blood vessel wall are complex and dynamic and that the nature of these interactions is altered by a variety of cardiovascular therapeutic interventions.
interactions between cells of the blood vessels and blood elements contribute to a number of important complications of cardiovascular interventions.

the pathophysiology of the vascular lesions associated with the various cardiovascular therapeutic interventions is complex, and that the pathobiological mechanisms involved are not completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

vascular lesion formation and its complications can be viewed as a series of events in which the cells of the blood vessels interact with the cells of the circulating blood and the cells of the implanted biomaterials in a manner that leads to the production of a vascular lesion.
the interactions between the blood vessel wall and the blood are complex and can lead to the formation of vascular lesions, which in turn, may lead to serious complications.
we have identified the molecular mechanisms by which blood-biomaterial interactions can lead to vascular lesion formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vascular lesions that form as a result of cardiovascular interventions can be influenced by interactions among blood elements, vascular cell functions, and biomaterials.

the blood is a dynamic, interactive system that can influence the behavior of the cells that make up blood vessel walls and that these interactions can contribute to the formation of lesions that limit the long term efficacy of many contemporary cardiovascular interventions.

the interactions of the vessel wall with the blood and with biomaterials are important determinants in the pathobiology of vascular lesions that develop in response to a variety of interventional therapies.
